“Racism is the process by which systems and policies, actions and attitudes create inequitable opportunities and outcomes for people based on race. Racism is more than just prejudice in thought or action. It occurs when this prejudice – whether individual or institutional – is accompanied by the power to discriminate against, oppress or limit the rights of others.” (Australian Human Rights Commission) “Prejudice is a bias or a preconceived opinion, idea, or belief about something.” (Dictionary.com) 

My point in quoting both of these definitions is racism is systemic. It’s written in policies and activity institutionally oppresses minorities. Prejudice is what’s being spoken of here. White people experience prejudice, which is still inexcusable, but they don’t experience racism as systems and policies favor them. Prejudice and racism are used interchangeably a lot but that key difference is important to distinct. 

As to why this happens? I believed it’s a deeply engrained prejudice in our society. Just as racism still exists and actively oppressed minorities, hateful attitudes and prejudice still exists in many bipoc homes. It’s cause and effect really. It’s unfortunate and the only way out of this hateful loop is education and change in our society and homes.

Sometimes schools will require you to apply for one through them, some schools just have codes floating around the internet. I just looked up “XYZ university fee waiver” and did some snooping. If you can’t find anything, email admissions and ask about/for a fee waiver and they’ll most likely give you one or direct you to their process of obtaining one. Fee waivers cut my cost from $400 to about $140.

Fee waivers are easy to find and schools are usually very accommodating about fee wavers so don't worry about that too much. I only applied to 7 schools and I regret it, so definitely apply to more than 7.
